$comment: Mission 1.70 §41, §42 and §58. The class decision, superseding the Mission 1.69 record without editing it.
why_no_artifact: §41 creates selected-quantity-class-v1.json only if Q1 becomes strategically viable. It did not.
why_no_construct: §42. Even a selected class stops before choosing the predicate, and no class was selected.

primary_outcome_reasoning.why_this_one: The external pair cannot form an honest common population — neither archive can be directed at a corpus, and neither documents whether its coverage means attempted or captured. An operator-run fetcher supplies both properties by construction, and the mechanism is one this repository already operates under review, so it is feasible in principle while its governance shape is genuinely new.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_A: Q1 is not strategically viable, so there is nothing to select.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_B_or_C: B and C report that the population problem is SOLVED, by pre-value co-coverage or by missingness preservation. Neither is solved; both fail on the same undocumented coverage semantics.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_E: E asserts the population architecture is INVALID because the only external route depends on post-hoc realized coverage. What was established is that the inclusion criteria are UNDOCUMENTED. Asserting invalidity would claim more than the evidence, which this repository has refused since Mission 1.60.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_F_or_G: F and G require one route's semantics to DOMINATE the blockage. The gap is symmetric: both routes leave attempted-versus-successful coverage undocumented, and naming one would misdescribe the finding.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_H: H needs an otherwise-viable route pair that is incompatible with commercial purpose. Neither route is established as incompatible, and the pair is not otherwise viable anyway.
primary_outcome_reasoning.why_not_I: I says evidence narrows without closing. The population question did close in one direction, and reporting it as open would discard that.
primary_outcome_reasoning.what_this_outcome_does_not_authorise: No measurement, no crawler, no HTTP request, and no governance approval. It names what a route would have to be.

requirement_registry.$comment: §43. A candidate emerged and is recorded rather than adopted, which is now the third mission running to apply that standard.

candidate_offered_and_not_added.name: COVERAGE_SEMANTICS_MUST_DISTINGUISH_ATTEMPT_FROM_SUCCESS
candidate_offered_and_not_added.candidate_meaning: Where an apparatus publishes a coverage surface, that surface must let a requester tell an entity that was never attempted from one that was attempted and produced no usable observation. Without it, any population defined by realized coverage may be conditioned on the measurement outcome, and the conditioning is undetectable from the published artifacts.
candidate_offered_and_not_added.why_it_is_distinct_from_SAMPLING_IS_LOAD: That rule asks the apparatus to disclose which eligible targets it attempted. This asks whether the published artifacts let an ANALYST reconstruct that distinction after the fact. An apparatus can disclose a sampling design in prose and still publish a coverage surface from which attempts and successes are indistinguishable, which is exactly the case here.
candidate_offered_and_not_added.why_it_was_not_added: Mission 1.67 set the standard when it adopted the previous candidate: a second independent instance in a DIFFERENT SHAPE. Common Crawl and HTTP Archive are two apparatuses in the same class exhibiting the same shape once. That is one instance seen twice.
candidate_offered_and_not_added.how_it_would_be_demonstrated: A second apparatus class where a coverage surface is published and attempt-versus-success remains indistinguishable — the scanner arc's frame findings are a plausible place to look, and this mission did not look, because §1 forbids reopening it.
candidate_offered_and_not_added.recorded_for: a future mission with the apparatus contract legitimately in scope

mission_accounting.value_exposure_note: Documentation pages carried illustrative examples — a sample index record and an example redirect target among them. None was used to choose or narrow a future predicate, and no predicate was chosen.

recommended_next_mission.recommended: Mission 1.71 — Bounded HTTP Measurement Governance & Apparatus Design V1
recommended_next_mission.scope: Whether SROS may become one measurement apparatus, and under what frozen contract. No crawl, and no measurement.
what_it_must_decide: whether the source-governance model can express a corpus of arbitrary public sites, which today it cannot, since every registered source is a named publisher
the frozen request contract a bounded fetcher would use
the robots and politeness rule, frozen rather than decided at runtime
how attempts and failures are recorded so missingness stays legible
the independence architecture against a named external apparatus
recommended_next_mission.the_residual_it_inherits: An operator fetcher fixes OUR side of the population problem and not the archive's. A pair would still need one archive whose attempt-level coverage is documented, and neither of the two currently is.
recommended_next_mission.do_not: restart broad quantity-class discovery, or reopen the scanner class
